request.spec:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the
cut as shown (empty when none).

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export pools (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-pools"`) to the Pools section, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The file starts with the header `pool,member,share,cut`, then has one line per member. Pools and their members come in the order they were added. A pool that is a member shows as `pool:<name>`, and a value containing a comma is quoted (e.g. `"Lee, Jo"`). The cut is exactly what the screen shows. It is empty when there is none, including for a member whose dates don't cover the sheet's today.

The change is only in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/pools/pools.ts`. The cuts are already worked out in the browser, so the export uses those instead of adding a server endpoint. That way the file can't disagree with the screen. It also reuses the existing `csvLine` helper and the same download approach as the people and claims exports.
